item.title: Spin generalizations of the classical elliptic Calogero--Inozemtsev model and integrable models of interacting tops associated with the $\rm{BC}_n$ root system
item.description: arXiv:2610.37165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct Lax pairs with a spectral parameter for a family of models of interacting tops associated with the $\rm{BC}_n$ root system. The construction uses the parametric $\rm{BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations, which involve both quantum $R$-matrices and boundary $K$-matrices satisfying the reflection equation. Special cases yield spin generalizations of the elliptic Calogero--Inozemtsev model. We also show how quantum Hamiltonians of interacting tops, combined with the Polychronakos freezing prescription, reproduce recently introduced anisotropic quantum long-range spin chains of Haldane--Shastry--Inozemtsev type.
item.dc:creator: D. Domanevsky, A. Zotov

item.title: The focusing coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with parallel nonzero boundary conditions: long--time asmptotics
item.description: arXiv:2610.37183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time behavior of solutions of the focusing coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with parallel constant nonzero boundary conditions in the solitonless setting. We distinguish three types of asymptotic regions: plane-wave regions, modulated elliptic-wave regions, and Painlev\'e-II transition regions. In each region, we derive the leading asymptotic term and the first correction, together with explicit error bounds. Our results show that, although localized perturbations may have components both parallel and orthogonal to the background, the leading asymptotic term is always parallel to the background vector. In particularly, in the elliptic-wave regions, the leading order is given by a scalar modulated elliptic wave multiplying the background vector, while the component of the solution orthogonal to the background is \(O(t^{-1/2})\). This is consistent with the linear stability analysis: the background is modulationally unstable to parallel perturbations but stable to orthogonal perturbations. The proof is based on applying the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest-descent method, together with a \(G\)-function mechanism, to the associated \(3\times3\) Riemann--Hilbert problem.
item.dc:creator: Haibing Zhang, Xianguo Geng, Bo Xue, Minxin Jia

item.title: Large number of hyperbolic and periodic solutions of sine-Gordon equation with nontrivial time dependence
item.description: arXiv:2610.36891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By using suitable ansatz which reduces the problem of obtaining exact solutions of the sine-Gordon equation with nontrivial time dependence to obtaining exact solutions of two first order symmetric $\phi^4$-like coupled equations in $x$ and $t$, we obtain a large number of hyperbolic and periodic solutions of the sine-Gordon equation. In particular, we not only obtain the well-known two-soliton, soliton-antisoliton and the breather solutions but also obtain periodic two-soliton, periodic soliton-antisoliton as well as periodic breather solutions. Besides, we also obtain superposed real and complex (parity-time reversal or) $\mathcal{PT}$-invariant solutions related to the two-soliton, soliton-antisoliton and the breather solutions of the sine-Gordon equation.
item.dc:creator: Thokala Soloman Raju, T. Shreecharan, Avinash Khare, Avadh Saxena

item.title: MPS overlaps and Sklyanin determinants
item.description: arXiv:2610.37285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive explicit overlap functions for integrable matrix product states associated with arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible evaluation representations of the orthogonal and symplectic twisted Yangians. The central step is to relate the commuting quasi-determinants entering the universal overlap formula to Sklyanin determinants of nested subalgebras. For orthogonal evaluation representations, this relation determines their spectra directly in the Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. In the symplectic case, we combine Sklyanin determinants and minors with a factorization of the nested rank-two boundary matrices to obtain the corresponding spectra. The resulting overlap functions are explicit products parametrized by Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns and require only the highest-weight data of the underlying orthogonal or symplectic representation. Together with the universal ratio of Gaudin determinants and the model-dependent pseudovacuum overlap coefficients, they determine the normalized MPS overlaps. We also express the overlap functions in the orthogonal case beyond evaluation representations in terms of the highest weights arising along the nested twisted-Yangian subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Tamas Gombor

item.title: Rank reduction in orthosymplectic types
item.description: arXiv:2610.37460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This note establishes a rank reduction for RLL-realization of quantum affine supergroups of orthosymplectic type. In the rational limit, this provides a more conceptual proof of the analogous result for orthosymplectic superYangians from arXiv:2311.18818. We also determine the exact scalar prefactor appearing in the evaluation of the universal $R$-matrix, refining the main result of arXiv:2408.16720.
item.dc:creator: Kyungtak Hong, Alexander Tsymbaliuk

item.title: GBDT with nontrivial seeds: explicit solutions of the focusing NLS equations and the corresponding Weyl functions
item.description: arXiv:2506.07702v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Our GBDT (generalised B\"acklund-Darboux transformation) approach is used to construct explicit solutions of the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation in the case of the exponential seed $a \exp\{2 i (cx +dt)\}$. The corresponding Baker-Akhiezer functions and evolution of the Weyl functions are obtained as well. In particular, the solutions, which appear in the study of rogue waves, step-like solutions and $N$-modulation solutions of the NLS equation are considered. This work is an essential development of our joint work with Rien Kaashoek and Israel Gohberg, where the seed was trivial, as well as several other of our previous works.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Sakhnovich
